'''Evelyn Algernon Valentine Ebsworth''', {{Post-nominals|country=GBR|CBE|FRSE|FRSC|size=100%|sep=,}} (14 February 1933 – 16 July 2015) was a British [[chemist]] and academic. He was the Crum Brown Professor of Chemistry at the [[University of Edinburgh]] from 1967 to 1990, and [[List of Vice-Chancellor & Wardens of Durham University|Vice-Chancellor and Warden]] of [[Durham University]] from 1990 to 1998.<ref name="Edinburgh Hon DSc">{{cite web|title=Professor Evelyn Algernon Valentine Ebsworth CBE, PhD, MA, ScD, DCL hc, FRSC, FRSE|url=http://www.chem.ed.ac.uk/about-us/tercentenary/tercentenary-events/tercentenary-graduation-ceremony/professor-evelyn-ebsworth|publisher=University of Edinburgh|accessdate=12 July 2014}}</ref><ref name="bio - Debrett's">{{cite web|title=Evelyn Algernon Valentine EBSWORTH|url=http://www.debretts.com/people-of-today/profile/10662/Evelyn-Algernon-Valentine-EBSWORTH|website=People of Today|publisher=Debrett's|accessdate=12 July 2014|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://archive.today/20140715084053/http://www.debretts.com/people-of-today/profile/10662/Evelyn-Algernon-Valentine-EBSWORTH|archivedate=15 July 2014}}</ref>

==Early life==
Ebsworth was born on 14 February 1933, [[Valentine's Day]], in [[Richmond, North Yorkshire|Richmond]], Yorkshire, England.<ref name="Edinburgh Hon DSc" /><ref name="bio - Debrett's" /> His father, [[Brigadier (United Kingdom)|Brigadier]] Wilfred Ebsworth,<ref name="obit - Independent">{{cite news|last1=Dalyell|first1=Tam|authorlink1=Tam Dalyell|title=Evelyn Ebsworth: One of the finest inorganic chemists of his generation|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/people/evelyn-ebsworth-one-of-the-finest-inorganic-chemists-of-his-generation-who-became-a-much-loved-a6668926.html|accessdate=12 October 2015|work=The Independent|date=27 September 2015}}</ref> served in the military during [[World War II]] and was posted to southern Africa. Ebsworth joined him on his posting and, from 1940 to 1945, lived in [[Southern Rhodesia]] and [[Kenya]]. He was educated at schools in many different countries before completing his education as a [[Boarding school|boarder]] at [[Marlborough College]], then an all-boys [[Private schools in the United Kingdom|Private school]] in [[Wiltshire]], England.<ref name="Edinburgh Hon DSc" />

In 1951, he matriculated into [[King's College, Cambridge]], where he studied chemistry. He graduated with a [[first class honours]] [[Bachelor of Arts]] (BA) degree in 1954.<ref name="bio - The Keynes Society">{{cite web|title=Evelyn Ebsworth|date=15 February 2010 |url=http://keynessociety.wordpress.com/who-ran-the-society/evelyn-ebsworth/|publisher=The Keynes Society|accessdate=12 July 2014}}</ref> This was promoted to a [[Master of Arts (Oxbridge and Dublin)|Master of Arts]] (MA) degree in 1958.<ref name="Edinburgh Hon DSc" /> He remained at the [[University of Cambridge]] to undertake [[post-graduate studies]]. He completed his [[Doctor of Philosophy]] (PhD) degree in 1957. His [[thesis]] was titled ''The preparation and properties of some silylamines'' and was supervised by [[Harry Julius Emeléus]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Evelyn Algernon Valentine Ebsworth|url=http://library.nd.edu/physics/resources/genealogy/chemistry/documents/EbsworthEAV.pdf|website=Hesburgh Libraries|publisher=University of Notre Dame|accessdate=12 July 2014|date=20 April 2010}}</ref>

During his university studies he was a member of the [[Cambridge Student Liberal Democrats|Cambridge University Liberal Club]]. He held a number of senior positions, including that of President during the 1954 [[Lent Term]].<ref name="bio - The Keynes Society" />

==Academic career==
Ebsworth was a [[junior research fellow]] at [[King's College, Cambridge]], from 1957 to 1959.<ref name="bio - The Keynes Society" /> He spent the last year of the fellowship at [[Princeton University]].<ref name="obit - Independent" /> In 1959, he moved to [[Christ's College, Cambridge]], where he had been elected a [[fellow]].<ref name="bio - Debrett's" /> He was a [[tutor]] at Christ's from 1964 to 1967.<ref name="Edinburgh Hon DSc" /> At university level, he was a [[List of academic ranks#United Kingdom|demonstrator]] from 1959 to 1964 and then a [[lecturer]] from 1964 to 1967.<ref name="bio - Debrett's" />

In 1967, he moved to the [[University of Edinburgh]] to take up the appointment of Crum Brown Professor of Chemistry.<ref name="bio - Debrett's" /> At the time of his appointment he was only 33 years old, unusually young for a [[Professor (highest academic rank)|professor]].<ref name="obit - Independent" /> He served as [[Dean (education)|dean]] of the Faculty of Science from 1984 to 1988.<ref name="Edinburgh Hon DSc" />

In 1990, he moved to [[Durham University]], where he had been appointed [[List of Vice-Chancellor & Wardens of Durham University|vice-chancellor and warden]].<ref name="bio - Debrett's" /> During his time as vice-chancellor, he oversaw the expansion of the university, including the completion of an additional [[campus]] based in [[Stockton-on-Tees]].<ref name="surprising story of Stockton">{{cite web|last1=Hayward|first1=John|title=Breaking the mold: the uprising story of Stockton|url=http://oxcheps.new.ox.ac.uk/MainSite%20pages/Resources/OxCHEPS_OP3.pdf|publisher=Oxford Centre for Higher Education Policy Studies|access-date=12 July 2014|archive-date=13 May 2006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060513190857/http://oxcheps.new.ox.ac.uk/MainSite%20pages/Resources/OxCHEPS_OP3.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

He retired from academia in 1998, and was appointed [[professor emeritus]] by Durham University.<ref name="bio - Debrett's" /><ref>{{cite web|title=Emeritus Titles|url=https://www.dur.ac.uk/university.calendar/archive/volumei/2012.2013/emeritus_titles/|publisher=Durham University|accessdate=12 July 2014}}</ref>

==Later life==
In 1998, Ebsworth created the [[Council for the Registration of Forensic Practitioners]] which accredited [[expert witnesses]].<ref name="bio - Debrett's" /><ref name="Edinburgh Hon DSc" /> He served as chairman of the council until 2005.<ref name="bio - Debrett's" /> From 2002 to 2012, he served as [[School governor|Chairman of Governors]] of two [[Private schools in the United Kingdom|private schools]] in Cambridge; [[St Faith's School]] and [[The Leys School]].<ref name="bio - Debrett's" />

In retirement, he lived in Cambridge, England.<ref name="bio - The Keynes Society" /> He died on 16 July 2015.<ref>[http://announcements.telegraph.co.uk/deaths/192958/ebsworth EBSWORTH]</ref>

==Personal life==
Ebsworth was twice married. In 1955, he married his first wife, Mary Salter. Together, they had three daughters and one son. Mary died in 1987. In 1990, he married Rose Zuckerman, an American. With this marriage came five [[stepchildren]].<ref name="obit - Independent" />

==Honours==
In 1969, Ebsworth was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Edinburgh]] (FRSE) and a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry]] (FRSC).<ref>{{cite web|title=Directory 2013/14|url=http://www.royalsoced.org.uk/cms/files/publications/directory/directory_nolist.pdf|publisher=The Royal Society of Edinburgh|accessdate=12 July 2014|archive-date=2 March 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140302044028/http://www.royalsoced.org.uk/cms/files/publications/directory/directory_nolist.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="Edinburgh Hon DSc" /> He was awarded the 1978 Main Group Chemistry Award by the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Main Group Chemistry Award Previous Winners|url=http://www.rsc.org/ScienceAndTechnology/Awards/MainGroupChemistryAward/PreviousWinners.asp|publisher=Royal Society of Chemistry|accessdate=12 July 2014}}</ref>

In 2002, he was awarded an [[honorary degree|honorary]] [[Doctor of Civil Law]] (DCL) degree by [[Durham University]].<ref name="bio - Debrett's" /> This was conferred upon him during a ceremony held at the Stockton campus of the university; a place that he himself had helped create.<ref name="surprising story of Stockton" /> In 2013, he was awarded an honorary [[Doctor of Science]] (ScD) degree by the [[University of Edinburgh]] 'in recognition of his major contribution to the growth in the study of Chemistry in Edinburgh'.<ref name="Edinburgh Hon DSc" />

In the 1996 [[Queen's Birthday Honours]], he was appointed [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) 'for services to higher education'.<ref name="LG 14 June 1996">{{London Gazette |issue=54427 |date=14 June 1996 |page=8 }}</ref>
